ess as resumable sessions, plus a Web panel to preview and file them.
# dsh-ai-import

Import the conversation history of other AI coding assistants into DeepSeek Harness (DSH) as
**resum
able sessions** — named after what was actually asked, and filed into one workspace per source.
Supported sources: **Claude Code**, **Codex CLI**, **WorkBuddy**, **Cursor**, and optionally **Trae*

*
(prompt-only). Two packages live in this repository:
| Package | Path | What it is |
| `dsh-ai-import` | root | the converter: scanning, naming, session writing, grouping, the `/import-

ai` command and two agent tools |
| `dsh-ai-import-ui` | `packages/ui` | the Web panel: a floating “
AI 导入” button, a right-hand drawer, and a three-column pick-and-file wizard |
The panel drives the same `scanAll()` / `runImport()` code and the same ledger as the command, so th

e
two can be used interchangeably.

Once published to npm the same two lines become `dsh plugin add dsh-ai-import` and
`dsh plugin add d

npm the same two lines become `dsh plugin add dsh-ai-import` and
`dsh plugin add dsh-ai-import-ui`.

Install both if you want the panel: `dsh-ai-import-ui` imports `dsh-ai-import/lib/*` directly and
do
es nothing useful without it. After installing, reload the DSH Web UI page.

Nothing in this plugin runs at install time — there is no build step, no `postinstall`, and no
depen
dency to compile. The packages ship plain ESM.

The same capability is exposed as two tools:

- `ai_import_scan({ detail: "summary" | "full" })`
- `ai_import_run({ sources?, dryRun?, force?, lim

mport_scan({ detail: "summary" | "full" })`
- `ai_import_run({ sources?, dryRun?, force?, limit? })`
## The Web panel

Click **AI 导入** in the bottom-right corner (it sits above the “🐳 Claude 迁移” button), or open
**Setti
ngs → AI 对话导入**. The drawer has two modes.

**Simple mode** — five source cards, each showing its resolved path (`手动指定` / `自动探测` /
`未找到`) and a

one-line tally `新增 N · 已导入 M · 过滤 K`. Tick the sources you want, optionally
tick *dry run* / *force*
, press **开始导入**, and watch a per-source progress bar and a result table.
**Pick mode (wizard)** — “上排三栏 + 下排整条预览”:
| Where | What | What you can do |
| top left | every source with new or changed conversations (`Codex（3）`) | click one; the middle col

umn lists its candidates |
| top middle | that source's candidates with checkboxes; for a folder, ar
chived sessions (grey, not checkable) followed by each source's unimported candidates | tick what to

import; click a row to preview it below |
| top right | every folder under `<DSH_HOME>/ai-import/gr
oups` plus an input + **建立** / **归档到** / **取消归档指定** | create a folder, or point the current selectio

n at an existing one |
| bottom, full width | the message stream of the selected conversation (quest
ion / answer / thinking / tool call) | decide whether this one is worth importing |

So “import three of these into an existing folder” is: click the folder, tick the conversations in
t
he middle column, press **归档到**, then **导入勾选的 N 条**.
## Naming
Titles come from, in order:

1. a title the source itself recorded — Claude's `custom-title` / `ai-title`, Codex's
`session_index

.jsonl` `thread_name`, a Cursor composer `name`;
2. the first line of the first human question, with

injected noise stripped (`<system-reminder>`,
`<user_info>`, `# AGENTS.md instructions`, `@skill:"…

`<source> <date time>`;
4. `<source> conversation N`.

Two traps that are handled explicitly: Codex's `thread_name` contains repeated automation titles
(`G

uardian review`, `Weekly review`, `hi`) — only names that appear exactly once in the whole index
are
trusted; and an unnamed Cursor composer stores a UUID in `name`, which is treated as no name.
## Grouping
One workspace per source, not per project:
| Source | Directory | Workspace title |

| Claude Code | `<DSH_HOME>/ai-import/groups/claude` | `Claude 对话` |
| Codex | `<DSH_HOME>/ai-import

/groups/codex` | `Codex 对话` |
| WorkBuddy | `<DSH_HOME>/ai-import/groups/workbuddy` | `WorkBuddy 对话`

|
| Cursor | `<DSH_HOME>/ai-import/groups/cursor` | `Cursor 对话` |
| Trae | `<DSH_HOME>/ai-import/gr
oups/trae` | `Trae 对话` |

A session's own `cwd` still points at the real project directory, so opening it in DSH carries the
r

ight project context; the group directory is used only when the original project is gone. The
wizard

can also file individual conversations into any subdirectory of `groups/`, and the folder
name beco
mes the workspace title.
## What it writes

- Sessions go through DSH's own `sessionPersistence` service, in the same on-disk format DSH uses
fo

r its own sessions, after passing `validateSessionEvents`, so they can be resumed normally.
- Every

session also gets a projection-cache record (`title` and `sessionListMetadata`), because
DSH's sessi

on list reads cold sessions from that cache — without the record an imported session
shows up as “未命

名” (untitled) until it is opened once.
- The ledger is `<DSH_HOME>/ai-import/imports.json`: source k

ey → session id, fingerprint, turns.
Re-running only picks up new or changed files; a source file th

at grew appends to its session
instead of creating a second one.
- Imported session ids look like `i

mport-claude-<uuid>`, namespaced by source so they cannot collide
with sessions imported by other to

t-claude-<uuid>`, namespaced by source so they cannot collide
with sessions imported by other tools.

Source files are only ever read. Nothing in the original assistant's directories is moved, renamed
o

es are only ever read. Nothing in the original assistant's directories is moved, renamed
or deleted.
## Requirements

- DSH `0.2.x` (the `engines.dsh` range in `package.json`).
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.9.0`.
- Offic
ial `@deepseek-ai/*` packages are declared as `peerDependencies`, not bundled.
